thread:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — providerX upstream egress instability detected from IAD region. Multiple prefixes showing AS-PATH oscillation and ~7-10% packet loss to customer-facing IPs. Auto-page oncall. @oncall
Alice Kim: grabbing it. seeing spikes in p99 and customer reports. tagging @Raj for routing.
Raj Patel: on it. initial traceroutes from IAD -> providerX show flip between two egress AS_PATHs, one containing AS60123 (providerX) and another that blackholes intermittently.
Leah Morris: customers in EU/US experiencing degraded embeddings latency ~300-800ms for a subset of requests. Support fielding first notices, no full outage yet. @Emily can you collect customer IDs affected?
Emily (Support): collecting now. so far 4 tenants reported errors and high latency, some 502s. I'll compile list and share.
Morgan (SRE): quick commands I ran:
```
# from iad-gw-2
traceroute -n 8.8.8.8
 1 10.0.0.1
 2 198.51.100.1
 3 203.0.113.5 (via AS60123)
 3 203.0.113.9 (via AS64500)
```
seeing alternating next-hops on repeated runs.
Diego Alvarez: also seeing BGP updates churn in the route table to our providerX peer. grabbing BGP logs.
incident-bot: BGP_UPDATE spike: 1200 updates/5m on session providerX (peer 203.0.113.1)
Raj Patel: can we temporarily prefer backup transit (providerY) for critical customer prefixes? We have spare capacity.
Alice Kim: yes — propose policy change: prepend AS on providerX route for affected prefixes to prefer providerY. Will need NOC approval and comms.
VendorX NOC: (automated) we are aware — investigating potential flaps on our edge. We see session resets correlated to your updates.
Leah Morris: risk check: traffic shift may increase cost and a bit more latency for other regions. but reduces packet loss. recommend proceed for critical prefixes only.
Raj Patel: plan: 1) prep export change (AS-path prepend providerX) for the 5 impacted prefixes 2) announce from providerY 3) monitor p99 and packetloss. rollback if errors.
Morgan (SRE): commands to push — will run canary on one prefix first. patch:
```
bgp-policy: set-prepend peer providerX prepend 3
apply to prefixes: 198.51.100.0/24 198.51.101.0/24
```
Alice Kim: executing canary on 198.51.100.0/24 now.
(reacted with :rotating_light: by Raj Patel)
Diego Alvarez: can confirm AS_PATH length increased toward providerX for canary prefix. traffic shifted to providerY within ~60s.
Emily (Support): customers for prefix 198.51.100.0/24 report improvement, 502s dropped. updating tickets.
VendorX NOC: we observe reduced churn for that prefix after your prepend. still investigating the root cause on our side.
Leah Morris: good — escalate to vendor engineering & keep monitoring for 30m. notify AMs for customers impacted.
Raj Patel: monitoring metrics: packet loss down from 8% -> 1.2% for canary. p99 latency improved ~220ms. proceeding to apply to remaining impacted prefixes.
Alice Kim: applying to remaining prefixes now. will keep tight watch; rollback if error.
incident-bot: INC-2026-1934567890: status -> mitigation in progress; assigned -> Alice Kim, Raj Patel; severity -> P1.
Morgan (SRE): post-mitigation checklist: 1) keep providerX session logs 2) collect BGP dumps 3) coordinate vendor postmortem 4) run traffic-tuning (batching) for affected routes if flux continues.
Emily (Support): sent customer updates: short summary + ETA for next update in 30m.
VendorX NOC: escalated to vendorX edge engineering — they will patch and engage peering ops. ETA initial finding 45m.
Alice Kim: thanks all. if we see any regression, immediate rollback and open comms. We'll update channel every 15 minutes.
(reacted with :thumbsup: by Leah Morris)
